findings.title: Scorecard test images are not pinned to immutable digests
findings.what: The release-gate tests execute quay.io/operator-framework/scorecard-test:v1.42.2 by tag. A tag can be moved or replaced upstream, allowing different code to run with no reviewed repository change and making scorecard results irreproducible.
findings.fix: Resolve v1.42.2 to its intended immutable manifest digest and change every image reference to quay.io/operator-framework/scorecard-test@sha256:<digest>.
findings.acceptance: Every scorecard image reference uses the expected sha256 digest, no scorecard-test tag-only reference remains in either patch, and rendering the scorecard configuration preserves that digest.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read every cited image field in the immutable baseline. All six executable entries are tag-only; neither dispatched patch supplies a digest or alternate immutable image reference.

findings.title: Artifact shipping permits plaintext transmission of bearer credentials and ~/.claude session data
findings.what: PROBAITIO_INGEST_URL is accepted without a scheme or destination policy. If configured with http://, shipOnce sends selected ~/.claude session artifacts and PROBAITIO_INGEST_TOKEN without transport encryption, exposing both sensitive content and the bearer credential to network interception.
findings.fix: Parse the configured URL at startup, reject non-HTTPS endpoints except an explicitly gated and narrowly validated local development mode, and apply an approved destination allowlist where required by egress policy.
findings.acceptance: Startup rejects an http:// ingest URL before reading or transmitting artifacts; an approved https:// URL succeeds; and an automated check confirms no request containing the ingest bearer or artifact body is issued for rejected URLs.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read URL normalization and the POST construction at the baseline. There is no protocol validation or TLS enforcement before the Authorization header and artifact body are passed to fetch; the file's own documented example also permits an http:// base URL.

findings.title: Single-file batches bypass the body cap and synchronously amplify up to 64 MiB artifacts
findings.what: The cap is checked only when batch.length > 0. Consequently, a first raw file of up to 64 MiB is always accepted even though base64 expands it to about 85.3 MiB, above the default 50 MiB cap and the stated approximately 64 MiB endpoint limit. The process then retains the raw buffer, base64 string, JSON string, and synchronous gzip output, causing large peak memory use and event-loop blocking in the sidecar.
findings.fix: Enforce the encoded-size budget for the first item too, choose a raw-file ceiling derived from envelope and base64 overhead, and stream or chunk encoding/compression rather than materializing all representations simultaneously.
findings.acceptance: A test using a 64 MiB eligible artifact proves it is chunked or rejected before whole-file base64/JSON/gzip materialization; emitted request bodies remain below the configured cap including envelope overhead; and measured peak RSS/event-loop delay stays within an explicit sidecar budget.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarially re-read collection and serialization in the immutable baseline and re-derived the expansion: 64 MiB × 4/3 is approximately 85.3 MiB before JSON overhead. The batch-cap condition explicitly exempts the first file, after which JSON.stringify and gzipSync add further whole-body allocations.
